query: (Cathay MD) Build a model to organise/optimise routes and service so Overall Rating > 7.

per_column.name: Service_Quality_Score
per_column.rationale: The 0.25-step values on a 1-5 scale indicate an average of the four service sub-ratings (Seat Comfort, Staff Service, Food & Beverages, Inflight Entertainment). These are reviewer-provided inputs that are correlated with, but NOT a deterministic function of, the separately-given Overall Rating, so aggregating them is a legitimate predictor of overall_rating_gt7. Marginal value is limited because the components already exist in the original table, but it is a valid predictive feature.

per_column.name: Service_to_Value_Gap
per_column.rationale: A signed difference (roughly service quality minus Value For Money) on a 0.25 grid. It encodes a discrepancy/interaction between two existing sub-ratings and plausibly carries predictive signal (mismatch between perceived service and value drives overall satisfaction). It is not a restatement of the focus nor knowable only after it, so it is a legitimate predictor.

per_column.name: Route_Complexity
per_column.rationale: Values 1/2/3 look like the number of legs/segments parsed from the Route string (direct vs. connecting). This is exogenous to the Overall Rating, is knowable before the outcome, and plausibly influences satisfaction (more connections -> lower rating). Genuinely new derived signal from the raw Route field.

per_column.name: Business_Traveller
per_column.rationale: Binary flag derived from Type of Traveller. Exogenous to the focus, available pre-outcome, and traveller segment plausibly correlates with rating propensity. A valid (if largely re-encoding an existing categorical) predictor.

per_column.name: Premium_Class
per_column.rationale: Binary indicator derived from Class (premium cabins vs. economy). Exogenous to the outcome and plausibly predictive of higher satisfaction. Legitimate predictor, though it mostly re-encodes the existing Class column.

per_column.name: High_Satisfaction
per_column.rationale: A near 50/50 binary explicitly named 'satisfaction' — almost certainly a re-thresholding of the Overall Rating (or of Recommended). That makes it a deterministic function / near-restatement of the focus variable itself; it would trivially and circularly 'predict' overall_rating_gt7. This is target leakage, not a usable feature.

judge.rationale: Five of the six columns are legitimate, non-leaking predictors, but most are deterministic re-encodings or aggregations of columns already present (service sub-ratings, Class, Type of Traveller), so their MARGINAL predictive leverage beyond the original table is modest. Route_Complexity is the clearest source of genuinely new signal, and Service_to_Value_Gap adds a useful interaction. High_Satisfaction is disqualifying leakage that restates the outcome and would inflate apparent performance. Net: a coherent, on-intent (service/route levers) feature set with moderate real incremental predictive value, dragged down by redundancy with originals and one leaky column.
